note: Everything this repository could not confirm from an official source, plus irregularities found while reviewing the repo. Published verbatim on the Flagged for Review page. Items here do not block the merge; they block assertion. Re-verified 2026-11-14 by session 0a3dff48: F-03 and F-12 were rewritten after a control test, and F-16/F-17 were added.

flags.title: Submitted tokens are not valid ASINs
flags.detail: B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3 and B00hJ57DV are each 9 characters. The ASIN identifier is 10 characters, so none of the three can address a catalog record as written. Each is alphanumeric, so only the length fails - consistent with a truncation, but the missing character is not recoverable and was not guessed.
flags.impact: Product identity, and every dependent field (title, brand, category, price, rating, commission band, competition), is unavailable.
flags.action_required: Re-supply the full 10-character ASIN or the complete amazon.<tld>/dp/<ASIN> URL for each item.

flags.title: Canonical product pages return Page Not Found
flags.detail: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B04G1MEwY , /dp/B02NbDxp3 and /dp/B00hJ57DV each returned Amazon's "Sorry! We couldn't find that page" error page when fetched on 2026-11-13.
flags.impact: Confirms the tokens do not exist in the catalog rather than merely being unresolvable from this network.
flags.action_required: None - evidence record. Re-verify if the ASINs are ever corrected.

flags.title: link.amazon short links resolve to one product each, but Amazon does not document the mapping
flags.detail: Measured 2026-11-13 and re-measured 2026-11-14: each submitted link resolves to exactly one destination ASIN, the same one on every fetch across both days - B04G1MEwY -> B0CDY277D3 (CHEFMAN 6 Quart Dual Basket Air Fryer Oven), B02NbDxp3 -> B09B7SB46R (Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door Air Fryer Toaster Oven), B00hJ57DV -> B08DKYBTPH (Chefman Air Fryer 8 Qt TurboFry). The earlier reading - that these were arbitrary 'fallback' pages - did not survive a control test: a bare, untagged request to a valid ASIN (/dp/B0CDY277D3) returns the same real product page and carries the same plpRedirect=mhFallback and lv=shuf markers, so those markers are not evidence of a fallback. What remains open is that no public Amazon document binds a link.amazon code to a destination ASIN, so the mapping is observed behaviour, not documented intent.
flags.impact: Product pages for B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R and B08DKYBTPH are accurate about those products (each row is traced to the manufacturer's own page), and these are the products the supplied links resolve to. They are not established as the items the brief named, because the brief named links, not ASINs.
flags.action_required: Owner: confirm the mapping in Associates Central and re-supply the 10-character ASINs if the intended items differ.

flags.title: link.amazon is not the documented public Associates short-link domain
flags.detail: The domain does resolve (it is served from Amazon CloudFront ranges), but it is not the public program's documented short-link domain used for Associates links; the public canonical product form is amazon.<tld>/dp/<ASIN> and program tooling provides its own link formats (S09). No Amazon help page surfaced in this review documents `link.amazon/<token>` as a publisher-facing link format.
flags.impact: Links of this shape cannot be relied on for tagging or attribution, and an untagged link earns nothing.
flags.action_required: Generate links from SiteStripe or the API in the tagged format required by the Participation Requirements (R-07).

flags.title: PA-API 5.0 is deprecated - the plan and most public tooling write-ups are stale
flags.detail: Amazon's legacy PA-API documentation URL now serves a deprecation notice: PA-API 5 calls return HTTP 403 with AccessDenied and instruct integrators to migrate to the Creators API. Amazon's own public Associates tools page (referenced in the site's source list) still describes the Product Advertising API as the programmatic option.
flags.impact: Any collector, tutorial, or dependency built against PA-API 5 will fail at runtime, not at build time. Architecture here targets the Creators API and degrades to a BLOCKED status rather than scraping.
flags.action_required: Register for Creators API access in Associates Central when the account exists (prerequisite: >=10 qualifying sales in the past 30 days, per Amazon's docs).

flags.title: No product may be marketed for these items until identity is verified
flags.detail: Because identity is unresolved, the article/comparison/guide generator is intentionally inert for all three entries. This blocks the "generate marketing content" step of the brief for these specific inputs.
flags.impact: Zero product copy is published for the three submitted links. Everything else in the platform (policy engine, rate data, scoring, tracking schema, templates, deploy) is delivered.
flags.action_required: Provide valid ASINs; the pipeline then produces verified-only content.

flags.title: No Associates account, marketplace, tracking ID, or tag supplied
flags.detail: The brief did not include an Associates ID/tag, target marketplace, or category access. Commission eligibility and reporting are account- and marketplace-specific, so no account-level figure can be verified or attributed.
flags.impact: Link builder runs in inert preview mode; earnings/conversion columns stay blank; the disclosure statement is still shown because it is required of every participant.
flags.action_required: Provide Associates ID + marketplace if live linking is wanted.

flags.title: No click, conversion, or earnings history exists
flags.detail: Nothing in the brief supplied a report export. Clicks are site-side and measurable after launch; conversion and earnings must come from Associates reporting under the Session definition (R-13).
flags.impact: All performance tables render as empty states with the ingestion contract documented, rather than illustrative numbers.
flags.action_required: Ingest a dated Associates report (or wire the earnings export) to activate the optimizer.

flags.title: Sandbox network allowlist limits live verification
flags.detail: The build environment may reach github.com, api.github.com, codeload.github.com, registry.npmjs.org and files.pythonhosted.org. Direct HTTPS to Amazon from that sandbox fails at TLS (curl SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL), so page evidence in this review was captured through the agent's fetch path and recorded with the final URL observed. Reproducing by hand needs only a browser.
flags.impact: Documented for auditability; does not change any conclusion.
flags.action_required: None.

flags.title: Repo review: prior merged site is honest but incomplete, and its citations predate these checks
flags.detail: Reviewed commit cfc04b1 (from arena/6b8bb130-zone2, merged via PR #1). Its three product rows are correctly blank/"Unverified" and all four of its cited reference URLs were re-fetched here and confirmed live and on-topic. Gaps: it links the deprecated PA-API overview without the deprecation notice, cites no commission rate table, no attribution window, no per-row official source, and has no category subpages.
flags.impact: Nothing published by that commit is wrong; the expansion here supplies what was missing. Its landing page, data.js rows and Pages workflow are preserved.
flags.action_required: Review the added pages; nothing from the merged commit was deleted.

flags.title: Policy pages carry different update dates and can change without notice
flags.detail: The Operating Agreement page states "Updated: October 15, 2025"; the Program Policies page states "Updated: April 14, 2026". Rates, Session mechanics and disclosure wording are all governed by pages Amazon may revise at any time, and the Agreement requires compliance with the most up-to-date version of the Program Policies.
flags.impact: Compliance data in this repository is timestamped and re-checked by the build; treat as a snapshot, not a subscription.
flags.action_required: Re-run tools/build_site.py --refresh before each publishing cycle.

flags.title: Reproducibility test: the redirect destination is stable, not a shuffled fallback
flags.detail: An earlier same-day re-fetch of https://link.amazon/B04G1MEwY was recorded as returning a different page body (a 'Best Sellers in Kitchen & Dining' carousel) and a different btn_ref token. That result is NOT reproducible and is withdrawn. Re-fetched on 2026-11-14, the link returns the same destination ASIN, the same product-page body and a stable per-link token, while a bare fetch of the same valid ASIN also carries plpRedirect=mhFallback and lv=shuf. The only element observed to vary between days is the per-request srctok attribution token (2026-11-13: srctok-1e229870efde5acf; 2026-11-14: srctok-1f979f303a4b5691 for B04G1MEwY), while the destination ASIN never changed. A rotating attribution token on a fixed destination is the behaviour of a tracked source link, not of a shuffle.
flags.impact: The published link-to-product mapping is reliable enough to build content about the three destination products. The residual risk is documentation, not behaviour: Amazon publishes no mapping for link.amazon codes.
flags.action_required: Owner: confirm the mapping in Associates Central; the three product pages may stay published as the products these links resolve to.

flags.title: Review note (resolved): one merged page title led with an Amazon mark
flags.detail: compliance.html in the research-hub namespace was titled 'Amazon rules this site complies with'. The Participation Requirements prohibit an Amazon mark in a domain name, subdomain, tag/Associates ID, or social identifier - a page title is none of those, and descriptive reference plus the mandated disclosure sentence are permitted. It was flagged because a title that opens with the mark can read as an official Amazon property, and Section 5 forbids implying endorsement or affiliation. Reworded on 2026-11-14 to 'Program rules this site complies with'; the build now emits 0 mark findings and 0 mark review notes.
flags.impact: No functional impact. The naming judgement call has been applied and the build warning is cleared.
flags.action_required: None - closed on 2026-11-14 by rewording the generated title.

flags.title: Duplicate of the prototype dashboard at northstar/ (disclosure gap since closed)
flags.detail: Commit 4bea98e added northstar/index.html, app.js, data.js and styles.css - a near-copy of the original Northstar dashboard - and the root files it was copied from were later removed, so the copy is now the only instance of that view. When measured against 9b8830d its served HTML carried no disclosure sentence (grep -c 'As an Amazon Associate' northstar/index.html -> 0). Re-measured on the merged tree after PR #3: the copy now carries the disclosure strip (count 1), so that gap is closed. Remaining point is structural: the primary site's footer links to northstar/index.html, so the duplicate is a live companion view rather than dead weight, and its content now drifts from the primary site's.
flags.impact: No compliance issue at measurement time on the merged tree. Two dashboard implementations now evolve independently; a reader following the footer link sees the older prototype with blank product rows.
flags.action_required: Optional: fold the prototype into the primary site, or label it explicitly as the earlier prototype in its own page heading so the difference is obvious to a reader.

flags.title: The hub's own verifier was stale after the namespace move (repaired 2026-11-14)
flags.detail: `python3 research-hub/scripts/verify.py` printed 7 failures on the tree it inherited: it computed its repository root as the script's parent directory (research-hub/), so it looked for research-hub/index.html, app.js, data.js and styles.css - files that live elsewhere or not at all - and it flagged research-hub/start.html's own ../zone2/index.html link as 'escaping the repository'. Its expected-file list also still named the pre-move root layout, and it treated the other sessions' assets as orphans. Repaired on 2026-11-14: it now resolves the repository root via parents[2], distinguishes hub-owned pages from pages owned by another session, and checks the hub's own required pages. It reports 3 products, 38 sourced attribute rows, 16 requirements, 13 pages and 0 errors, and it now runs in CI on every push and pull request.
flags.impact: Resolved. The hub's rows are policed again by the guard that was written for them: an unsourced 'verified' row added to research-hub/data/products.json now fails the build.
flags.action_required: None - closed on 2026-11-14.

flags.title: The per-ASIN commission rate cannot be confirmed without a signed-in Associates account
flags.detail: Amazon's public Associates Program Standard Commission Income Statement (Table 1) IS readable without signing in and publishes a fixed rate for every category band - including 'Physical Books, Kitchen, Automotive' at 4.50% and 'Toys, Furniture, Home, Home Improvement, ...' at 3.00%, the two rows that together make up the Home & Kitchen department. The account-specific rate card (https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/schedule) redirects to Amazon sign-in (customratecard), so the rate that Amazon actually applies to a given ASIN for a given account cannot be read from a public page.
flags.impact: Category-band rates are published as sourced facts. The rate actually paid on each individual product stays blank and flagged rather than being inferred from a band.
flags.action_required: Owner: read the per-ASIN rate from the account's own Associates Central earnings report, or from SiteStripe's Product Links.

flags.title: The per-request srctok attribution token rotates while the destination stays fixed
flags.detail: Each supplied link returns a distinct per-link token of the form btn_ref=srctok-<16 hex>. The three tokens are different from each other and identical on same-day re-fetch, but they differ between 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14 for the same link (B04G1MEwY: srctok-1e229870efde5acf -> srctok-1f979f303a4b5691), while the destination ASIN did not change on any fetch across five sessions and two days.
flags.impact: Confirms the links are individually tracked source links. It also means the token must not be treated as a stable identifier of the link - only the destination ASIN is stable.
flags.action_required: None - recorded so no later reviewer mistakes token rotation for destination instability.

flags.title: The research-hub generator deleted its own 16 generated pages and then crashed
flags.detail: `research-hub/scripts/build.py` removed the hub's generated output first and only then tried to read docs/executive-summary.md from inside the research-hub namespace, where the document no longer lives (it had moved to the repository root during the namespace move). The run therefore left the hub with no pages and an error. It also emitted pre-move link paths - index.html and zone2/index.html - which do not resolve from research-hub/, so even a successful rebuild would have produced broken links. Anyone who ran the build would have destroyed the hub.
flags.impact: Data loss in the generated namespace and broken navigation if the generator is run. It was not run by CI at the time, so the committed pages were unaffected - the damage was latent.
flags.action_required: Closed on 2026-11-14: the document is resolved from the repository root, the emitted paths are post-move, and `python3 research-hub/scripts/build.py --check` builds into a temporary directory to prove the committed output matches a fresh build without touching it. The check runs in CI.

flags.title: Conflict: Emeril Lagasse model number differs between the Amazon listing and the manufacturer's store
flags.detail: For the product the supplied link https://link.amazon/B02NbDxp3 resolves to (amazon.com/dp/B09B7SB46R), the Amazon listing gives model number 4-00675-02X-VN while the manufacturer's own store gives 4-00675-02A-VN for the French Door AirFryer 360, 26 QT. Both official pages are cited side by side; neither is presented as definitive. The manufacturer figure is the one carried in the spec table, with the Amazon figure beside it.
flags.impact: No functional impact. A model-number mismatch is the kind of thing that breaks warranty lookups and parts matching, so it is recorded for the owner.
flags.action_required: Optional: confirm which model number the sold unit carries in Associates Central / the supplier invoice. Both values are published; neither is asserted.

flags.title: Conflict: CHEFMAN 6 Qt capacity is stated in two different units, and one Amazon page disagrees with itself
flags.detail: Chefman's product page for model RJ38-SQPF-3TDB-2W states Capacity 6 Qt / 5.67 L. On Amazon's page for B0CDY277D3 the listing title says '2 Independent 3Qt' baskets and the Size field says 6 Quart, but the product-information Capacity field says 6 liters - and 6 qt is 5.67 L, so the two Amazon fields on that one page disagree with each other. Both readings are published on the primary site and in research-hub; neither is presented as definitive. Re-verified 2026-11-14 by fetching the Amazon product-information and item-details blocks directly.
flags.impact: No functional impact. A capacity figure is what a buyer compares, so a 6 qt vs 6 L difference matters to anyone using the spec to judge whether the appliance is big enough.
flags.action_required: Optional: the manufacturer figure (6 qt / 5.67 L) is the one carried first; confirm the unit on the retail carton if the owner needs one number.

flags.title: Two blank fields were described as unverified when they are in fact withheld by policy
flags.detail: Price, star rating, review count and availability were published as blank because 'no official source confirms them'. That was inaccurate: re-fetching the three destination pages on 2026-11-14 shows list prices, star ratings, review counts and stock status plainly present on the official Amazon pages (for example 4.3/18,320 on B09B7SB46R and 4.4/16,863 on B08DKYBTPH). They are blank because Program Policies §6(a) forbids altering Program Content, §6(t) forbids displaying customer reviews or star ratings unless they are obtained through Creators API or PA API, and §6(y) bars price-tracking and price-alerting functionality on the site; under the IP License that content is obtained through the API.
flags.impact: No published value changed - the cells are still blank. What changed is the stated reason, on the primary site, in affiliate-lab, in revalidation and on the Flagged for Review page, so that a reviewer does not read a policy decision as a verification failure.
flags.action_required: None - the reason is now stated accurately and each of the two reasons is flagged separately on every surface that publishes the blank cells.
